// RFC 4180 CSV parser. Fields are separated by `delimiter`, records by CRLF or LF. A field may be quoted with `"`;
// inside quotes, delimiters and line breaks are literal and `""` is an escaped quote. A quote inside an unquoted field
// is literal. A trailing line break at the end of the input does not start a new record. An unterminated quoted
// field is an error reported at the line where the field starts.

export class CsvError extends Error {
  constructor(message, line) {
    super(`${message} (line ${line})`);
    this.line = line;
  }
}

export function parse(text, { delimiter = "," } = {}) {
  const records = [];
  let record = [];
  let field = "";
  let inQuotes = false;
  let wasQuoted = false;
  let recordOpen = false;
  let line = 1;
  let quoteStartLine = 1;
  let i = 0;

  const endField = () => {
    record.push(field);
    field = "";
    wasQuoted = false;
  };
  const endRecord = () => {
    endField();
    records.push(record);
    record = [];
    recordOpen = false;
  };

  while (i < text.length) {
    const c = text[i];
    if (inQuotes) {
      if (c === '"') {
        if (text[i + 1] === '"') {
          field += '"';
          i += 2;
        } else {
          inQuotes = false;
          i++;
        }
      } else {
        if (c === "\n") line++;
        field += c;
        i++;
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (c === '"' && field === "" && !wasQuoted) {
      inQuotes = true;
      wasQuoted = true;
      recordOpen = true;
      quoteStartLine = line;
      i++;
    } else if (c === delimiter) {
      endField();
      recordOpen = true;
      i++;
    } else if (c === "\r" && text[i + 1] === "\n") {
      endRecord();
      line++;
      i += 2;
    } else if (c === "\n") {
      endRecord();
      line++;
      i++;
    } else {
      field += c;
      recordOpen = true;
      i++;
    }
  }
  if (inQuotes) throw new CsvError("unterminated quoted field", quoteStartLine);
  if (recordOpen) endRecord();
  return records;
}

All 22 tests pass. Here's a summary of what was wrong and what I changed:

## Root-cause fixes in `src/parse.js`

The code diverged from the behaviour described in the header comment in four places:

1. **Escaped quotes ignored** — inside a quoted field, any `"` closed the quote, so `""` (an escaped quote per the spec) wasn't handled. Now, a `"` inside a quoted field is checked against the next character: `""` appends a literal `"` and stays in the quoted state; a single `"` closes the field.
2. **CRLF not a line terminator** — `\r` was treated as an ordinary character, so `a,b\r\n` produced fields like `b\r`. Added a branch that terminates the record on `\r\n` (consuming both characters, incrementing the line count once). A lone `\r` remains literal, matching the spec comment ("records by CRLF or LF").
3. **Wrong error line for unterminated quotes** — the error was reported at the *current* line (EOF) instead of the line where the quoted field *started*. Now `quoteLine` is captured when the opening quote is seen and used in the `CsvError`.
4. **Trailing-record heuristic broken** — the old `if (field !== "") endRecord()` decided "is there a pending record?" by the field's content, which silently dropped records whose last field is empty (e.g. `parse("a,,")` returned `[["a"]]`). Replaced with a `recordOpen` flag set whenever any input contributes to the current record and cleared on `endRecord`. This also keeps `parse("") → []` and "trailing line break doesn't start a new record" working.

No test expectations were changed, and nothing is special-cased — the changes are the general state-machine fixes.

## New edge-case tests (`test/parse.test.js`)

- trailing record without a line break (`parse("a,b")`)
- trailing empty fields without a line break (`parse("a,,")` — the `recordOpen` fix)
- empty input; single empty line → one empty record
- CRLF without a trailing line break
- lone CR is literal, both unquoted and quoted
- CRLF inside quotes is literal
- quote inside an unquoted field is literal
- quoted empty field
- custom delimiter
- unterminated quote: at line 1, after earlier lines, and spanning a line break (start line reported)
- `parseObjects` with header-only or empty input
